title: A Mixtape for the Detention
premise: Odile Underhill has spent senior year keeping his head down, channeling everything he can't say into the loaves he bakes at his family's bakery—until history teacher Ms. Vann pairs him with Priya Kestrel, the debate captain who got him suspended freshman year, for a project documenting the town's dying tradition of the Harvest Mixtape, a cassette of songs played before every fall football game. As they interview old-timers and uncover that the school board plans to sell the field—and erase the tradition—to a developer, Odile and Priya's reluctant partnership turns into something neither will name. When Odile learns his own father once traded away the original master tape to save the bakery, he must choose between protecting his family's secret and playing the recovered recording at the final game. In the end, the tape plays over the loudspeakers as the town floods the field, the sale collapses, and Odile finally bakes a loaf with his own name on it.
about_author: I. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former small-town radio DJ who spent three years archiving obsolete cassettes from community centers across the Midwest. They write stories about kids who find their voices in places everyone else has stopped listening.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Opening week of senior semester: Odile bakes grief-bread after his grandmother's funeral and keeps his world to flour, ovens, and countdown calendars. Ms. Vann assigns the Heritage Project, pairing him with Priya Kestrel, his oldest enemy. Their first meeting in the library ends in a shouting match over who ruined whose reputation. Emotional beat: claustrophobic resentment—the story's locked door.

chapters.title: Side A
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced together by the project, they interview elderly residents about the Harvest Mixtape and discover the tradition began as a love letter broadcast illegally in 1974. Priya shows unexpected vulnerability; Odile finds her handwritten apology she never sent. Meanwhile, Odile overhears the school board discussing selling the field. Emotional beat: thawing—enemy becomes ally, first crack of attraction.

chapters.title: The Last Game
chapters.summary: Priya's POV dominates. The pair locates the original master tape in a storage unit belonging to Odile's father—who confesses he sold it years ago to keep the bakery alive during bankruptcy. Feeling betrayed by both the town's myth and his dad, Odile nearly quits. The developer's offer goes public, splitting the town. Emotional beat: betrayal and reckoning—the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Baked With Love
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the final game, with the board poised to vote, Odile and Priya hijack the PA system and play the crackling 1974 tape; the crowd falls silent, then sings along, and the vote collapses under public pressure. Father and son reconcile over the truth. Priya and Odile finally kiss in the emptying parking lot. Epilogue image: a new loaf labeled 'Underhill & Kestrel.' Emotional beat: release—love chosen over duty, memory saved.
